title: Voluntary Provident Fund: Should You Invest Beyond EPF?
description: Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF) allows salaried employees to contribute more than the mandatory 12% to their Provident Fund account. VPF offers the same intere.

faq.q: What is the difference between EPF and VPF?
faq.a: EPF is a mandatory contribution from both employee and employer, while VPF is an additional, voluntary contribution made only by the employee, over and above the mandatory EPF. Both earn the same interest rate.

Interest earned on employee contributions to EPF and VPF up to ₹2.5 lakh in a financial year remains tax-free. Interest on contributions exceeding this limit is now taxable. For accounts without employer contributions, the limit is ₹5 lakh.

faq.q: Can I withdraw VPF funds anytime?
faq.a: No, VPF follows the same withdrawal rules as EPF. Full withdrawal is typically allowed only upon retirement or extended unemployment. Partial withdrawals are permitted under specific conditions like medical emergencies or housing needs, subject to certain criteria.

faq.q: Are VPF contributions eligible for Section 80C deduction?
faq.a: Yes, your contributions to VPF are eligible for tax deduction under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, within the overall annual limit of ₹1.5 lakh, similar to EPF contributions.

faq.q: How do I start contributing to VPF?
faq.a: You need to inform your employer's HR or payroll department about your decision to contribute to VPF and specify the percentage of your basic salary you wish to contribute. They will then deduct the amount from your salary.

faq.q: Is there a limit to how much I can contribute to VPF?
faq.a: You can contribute up to 100% of your basic salary plus dearness allowance to VPF, over and above your mandatory EPF contribution. However, the tax-free interest limit on employee contributions remains ₹2.5 lakh (or ₹5 lakh if no employer contribution).
